Arrows join the timeline's four stages (Screens 1 and 2), so students read them as one process rather than separate options.
Each question and its answer share a box (Screens 2 to 6), and related prompts share a group (Screens 7 and 8), so it's clear what belongs together.
Screen headings are largest, thick borders mark the key item on a screen, such as a decision point, and darker filled buttons mark the main action.
